blocks.text: What RabbitMQ is
blocks.html: What RabbitMQ is

blocks.text: RabbitMQ is a message broker: a server that accepts messages from applications and delivers them to other applications.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ is a message broker: a server that accepts messages from applications and delivers them to other applications.

blocks.text: The sending application is a producer. The receiving application is a consumer.
blocks.html: The sending application is a producer. The receiving application is a consumer.

blocks.text: The applications can work asynchronously: the producer sends a message without waiting for the consumer to finish the work.
blocks.html: The applications can work asynchronously: the producer sends a message without waiting for the consumer to finish the work.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ handles routing, buffering, and delivery. The consumer application performs the requested work.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ handles routing, buffering, and delivery. The consumer application performs the requested work.

blocks.text: These notes explain exchanges and queues using the AMQP 0-9-1 messaging model. RabbitMQ also supports other protocols and streams.
blocks.html: These notes explain exchanges and queues using the AMQP 0-9-1 messaging model. RabbitMQ also supports other protocols and streams.

blocks.text: Messages
blocks.html: Messages

blocks.text: A message carries data from one application to another. Its meaning is defined by the applications.
blocks.html: A message carries data from one application to another. Its meaning is defined by the applications.

blocks.text: It can request an action, such as sending an email, resizing an image, charging a payment, or generating an invoice.
blocks.html: It can request an action, such as sending an email, resizing an image, charging a payment, or generating an invoice.

blocks.text: It can also report an event, such as an order being placed. Messages are not limited to commands or tasks.
blocks.html: It can also report an event, such as an order being placed. Messages are not limited to commands or tasks.

blocks.text: The message body contains the application data. Properties and headers can carry information such as a message ID, content type, or application-defined attributes.
blocks.html: The message body contains the application data. Properties and headers can carry information such as a message ID, content type, or application-defined attributes.

blocks.text: Let us say an order service sends an order ID. An invoice service receives the message and uses that ID to generate an invoice.
blocks.html: Let us say an order service sends an order ID. An invoice service receives the message and uses that ID to generate an invoice.

blocks.text: The message flow
blocks.html: The message flow

blocks.text: The usual flow is: Producer → Exchange → Queue → Consumer.
blocks.html: The usual flow is: Producer → Exchange → Queue → Consumer.

blocks.text: The producer publishes a message to an exchange, with routing information.
blocks.html: The producer publishes a message to an exchange, with routing information.

blocks.text: The exchange applies routing rules and sends the message to matching queues.
blocks.html: The exchange applies routing rules and sends the message to matching queues.

blocks.text: A queue stores messages until they can be delivered and handled according to its acknowledgement and retention rules.
blocks.html: A queue stores messages until they can be delivered and handled according to its acknowledgement and retention rules.

blocks.text: A consumer receives a message, interprets it, and processes it. RabbitMQ does not perform the business action itself.
blocks.html: A consumer receives a message, interprets it, and processes it. RabbitMQ does not perform the business action itself.

blocks.text: Exchanges, bindings, and routing keys
blocks.html: Exchanges, bindings, and routing keys

blocks.text: An exchange routes messages. It is not the buffer where messages wait for consumers.
blocks.html: An exchange routes messages. It is not the buffer where messages wait for consumers.

blocks.text: A binding connects an exchange to a queue and supplies any matching rules needed by the exchange type.
blocks.html: A binding connects an exchange to a queue and supplies any matching rules needed by the exchange type.

blocks.text: A routing key is a label supplied by the producer. Some exchange types use it to select queues.
blocks.html: A routing key is a label supplied by the producer. Some exchange types use it to select queues.

blocks.text: Routing can send a message to one queue or several queues. Each matching queue receives its own copy.
blocks.html: Routing can send a message to one queue or several queues. Each matching queue receives its own copy.

blocks.text: Bindings let routing change without changing the producer, provided its publishing contract stays the same.
blocks.html: Bindings let routing change without changing the producer, provided its publishing contract stays the same.

blocks.text: The producer still needs to know where to publish. Decoupling does not mean that it knows nothing about routing.
blocks.html: The producer still needs to know where to publish. Decoupling does not mean that it knows nothing about routing.

blocks.text: The default exchange automatically routes to a queue when the routing key matches its name. This looks like sending directly to a queue, but an exchange is still involved.
blocks.html: The default exchange automatically routes to a queue when the routing key matches its name. This looks like sending directly to a queue, but an exchange is still involved.

blocks.text: If no queue matches, RabbitMQ can discard the message. A publisher can request a return for an unroutable message, or an alternate exchange can provide another routing path.
blocks.html: If no queue matches, RabbitMQ can discard the message. A publisher can request a return for an unroutable message, or an alternate exchange can provide another routing path.

blocks.text: Exchange types
blocks.html: Exchange types

blocks.text: Direct: matches the message’s routing key exactly against binding keys. For example, an invoice binding receives messages labelled invoice.
blocks.html: Direct: matches the message’s routing key exactly against binding keys. For example, an invoice binding receives messages labelled invoice.

blocks.text: Fanout: sends a copy to every bound queue and ignores the routing key. This supports broadcasting to independent subscribers.
blocks.html: Fanout: sends a copy to every bound queue and ignores the routing key. This supports broadcasting to independent subscribers.

blocks.text: Topic: matches routing keys against patterns of dot-separated words. A single-word wildcard (*) matches one word; a multi-word wildcard (#) matches zero or more words.
blocks.html: Topic: matches routing keys against patterns of dot-separated words. A single-word wildcard (*) matches one word; a multi-word wildcard (#) matches zero or more words.

blocks.text: For example, order.* matches order.created, while order.# can also match order.payment.failed.
blocks.html: For example, order.* matches order.created, while order.# can also match order.payment.failed.

blocks.text: Headers: matches message header values against binding rules instead of using the routing key.
blocks.html: Headers: matches message header values against binding rules instead of using the routing key.

blocks.text: Queues and consumers
blocks.html: Queues and consumers

blocks.text: A queue is managed by RabbitMQ. It can buffer messages while consumers are busy or disconnected, subject to configured limits and lifetime.
blocks.html: A queue is managed by RabbitMQ. It can buffer messages while consumers are busy or disconnected, subject to configured limits and lifetime.

blocks.text: A consumer usually subscribes, and RabbitMQ delivers messages over that subscription. Applications can also explicitly fetch messages.
blocks.html: A consumer usually subscribes, and RabbitMQ delivers messages over that subscription. Applications can also explicitly fetch messages.

blocks.text: With manual acknowledgements, messages can be ready for delivery or delivered but still unacknowledged.
blocks.html: With manual acknowledgements, messages can be ready for delivery or delivered but still unacknowledged.

blocks.text: A ready message is waiting for a consumer. An unacknowledged message has been delivered, but RabbitMQ is still waiting for confirmation.
blocks.html: A ready message is waiting for a consumer. An unacknowledged message has been delivered, but RabbitMQ is still waiting for confirmation.

blocks.text: Prefetch limits the number of outstanding unacknowledged deliveries for a consumer. It helps prevent a consumer from receiving more work than it can handle.
blocks.html: Prefetch limits the number of outstanding unacknowledged deliveries for a consumer. It helps prevent a consumer from receiving more work than it can handle.

blocks.text: An unacknowledged message does not necessarily stop later messages from being delivered. Delivery continues when consumer capacity and prefetch allow it.
blocks.html: An unacknowledged message does not necessarily stop later messages from being delivered. Delivery continues when consumer capacity and prefetch allow it.

blocks.text: Acknowledgements
blocks.html: Acknowledgements

blocks.text: A consumer acknowledgement tells RabbitMQ that a delivery has been handled. RabbitMQ trusts this signal; it cannot check whether the business work actually succeeded.
blocks.html: A consumer acknowledgement tells RabbitMQ that a delivery has been handled. RabbitMQ trusts this signal; it cannot check whether the business work actually succeeded.

blocks.text: With automatic acknowledgement, RabbitMQ considers a message handled when it sends the delivery. A consumer failure before processing finishes can lose that work.
blocks.html: With automatic acknowledgement, RabbitMQ considers a message handled when it sends the delivery. A consumer failure before processing finishes can lose that work.

blocks.text: With manual acknowledgement, the application chooses when to acknowledge. It normally does so after successful processing.
blocks.html: With manual acknowledgement, the application chooses when to acknowledge. It normally does so after successful processing.

blocks.text: After acknowledgement, the queue can remove the message. Receiving a message alone does not complete this lifecycle in manual acknowledgement mode.
blocks.html: After acknowledgement, the queue can remove the message. Receiving a message alone does not complete this lifecycle in manual acknowledgement mode.

blocks.text: A consumer can reject a delivery and request requeueing, or reject it without requeueing.
blocks.html: A consumer can reject a delivery and request requeueing, or reject it without requeueing.

blocks.text: A message rejected without requeueing can be sent through a configured dead-letter exchange for separate handling; otherwise it is discarded.
blocks.html: A message rejected without requeueing can be sent through a configured dead-letter exchange for separate handling; otherwise it is discarded.

blocks.text: Messages can also be removed by expiration, queue limits, or administrative actions. Acknowledgement is not the only removal mechanism.
blocks.html: Messages can also be removed by expiration, queue limits, or administrative actions. Acknowledgement is not the only removal mechanism.

blocks.text: Consumer failure and redelivery
blocks.html: Consumer failure and redelivery

blocks.text: Assume a consumer receives a message with manual acknowledgement enabled.
blocks.html: Assume a consumer receives a message with manual acknowledgement enabled.

blocks.text: If its channel or connection closes before acknowledgement, RabbitMQ normally makes the outstanding delivery available again.
blocks.html: If its channel or connection closes before acknowledgement, RabbitMQ normally makes the outstanding delivery available again.

blocks.text: Another eligible consumer, or the original consumer after reconnecting, can receive it.
blocks.html: Another eligible consumer, or the original consumer after reconnecting, can receive it.

blocks.text: Not receiving an acknowledgement immediately does not itself mean failure. The consumer may still be processing; connection failure or an acknowledgement timeout can trigger recovery.
blocks.html: Not receiving an acknowledgement immediately does not itself mean failure. The consumer may still be processing; connection failure or an acknowledgement timeout can trigger recovery.

blocks.text: If the consumer completed the action but failed before acknowledging, the action may run again on redelivery.
blocks.html: If the consumer completed the action but failed before acknowledging, the action may run again on redelivery.

blocks.text: A message that repeatedly fails needs a controlled retry policy and a separate failure-handling path. Requeueing forever can waste capacity.
blocks.html: A message that repeatedly fails needs a controlled retry policy and a separate failure-handling path. Requeueing forever can waste capacity.

blocks.text: Delivery guarantees and safe retries
blocks.html: Delivery guarantees and safe retries

blocks.text: Automatic acknowledgement can give at-most-once handling of a queued delivery: the application may miss work after a failure.
blocks.html: Automatic acknowledgement can give at-most-once handling of a queued delivery: the application may miss work after a failure.

blocks.text: Manual acknowledgement and redelivery support at-least-once processing when messages remain available and failures are retried. Duplicate processing is possible.
blocks.html: Manual acknowledgement and redelivery support at-least-once processing when messages remain available and failures are retried. Duplicate processing is possible.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ alone does not guarantee that an arbitrary business action happens exactly once.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ alone does not guarantee that an arbitrary business action happens exactly once.

blocks.text: Consumers should handle repeated deliveries safely. An idempotent operation has the same intended effect when the same request is repeated.
blocks.html: Consumers should handle repeated deliveries safely. An idempotent operation has the same intended effect when the same request is repeated.

blocks.text: For example, the consumer can use a stable request identifier to recognise work already completed. The duplicate check must be coordinated with the action; a separate check can itself fail midway.
blocks.html: For example, the consumer can use a stable request identifier to recognise work already completed. The duplicate check must be coordinated with the action; a separate check can itself fail midway.

blocks.text: A delivery is not proof that processing succeeded, and an acknowledgement is not proof that no earlier attempt performed the action.
blocks.html: A delivery is not proof that processing succeeded, and an acknowledgement is not proof that no earlier attempt performed the action.

blocks.text: Durability, persistence, and publisher confirms
blocks.html: Durability, persistence, and publisher confirms

blocks.text: Durability describes whether a queue survives a broker restart. A durable queue alone does not make every message persistent.
blocks.html: Durability describes whether a queue survives a broker restart. A durable queue alone does not make every message persistent.

blocks.text: For classic queues, important messages need persistent delivery mode as well as a durable queue. A non-durable queue can disappear on restart even if its messages were marked persistent.
blocks.html: For classic queues, important messages need persistent delivery mode as well as a durable queue. A non-durable queue can disappear on restart even if its messages were marked persistent.

blocks.text: Publisher confirms let the producer learn that RabbitMQ has accepted responsibility for a published message according to the destination queue’s guarantees.
blocks.html: Publisher confirms let the producer learn that RabbitMQ has accepted responsibility for a published message according to the destination queue’s guarantees.

blocks.text: A publisher confirm is separate from a consumer acknowledgement. It does not mean a consumer has processed the message.
blocks.html: A publisher confirm is separate from a consumer acknowledgement. It does not mean a consumer has processed the message.

blocks.text: If the connection fails before confirmation arrives, the producer may not know whether the message was accepted. Retrying can create a duplicate.
blocks.html: If the connection fails before confirmation arrives, the producer may not know whether the message was accepted. Retrying can create a duplicate.

blocks.text: Important messages need appropriate queue durability, persistence, publisher confirms, routing checks, and consumer acknowledgements. No single setting covers every failure.
blocks.html: Important messages need appropriate queue durability, persistence, publisher confirms, routing checks, and consumer acknowledgements. No single setting covers every failure.

blocks.text: Queue replication protects against some broker failures. Classic queues are not replicated; quorum queues keep replicated data across brokers.
blocks.html: Queue replication protects against some broker failures. Classic queues are not replicated; quorum queues keep replicated data across brokers.

blocks.text: A quorum queue needs a majority of its replicas available to operate. Replication improves resilience but does not protect against every combination of failures.
blocks.html: A quorum queue needs a majority of its replicas available to operate. Replication improves resilience but does not protect against every combination of failures.

blocks.text: Competing consumers
blocks.html: Competing consumers

blocks.text: Several consumers can receive work from the same queue. RabbitMQ distributes deliveries among eligible consumers.
blocks.html: Several consumers can receive work from the same queue. RabbitMQ distributes deliveries among eligible consumers.

blocks.text: A normal delivery goes to one consumer, so workers share the work rather than each receiving every message.
blocks.html: A normal delivery goes to one consumer, so workers share the work rather than each receiving every message.

blocks.text: Adding workers can increase processing capacity when the work can run in parallel. Actual distribution depends on consumer capacity and delivery settings.
blocks.html: Adding workers can increase processing capacity when the work can run in parallel. Actual distribution depends on consumer capacity and delivery settings.

blocks.text: This is not a promise of exactly-once processing: failures can still cause the same message to be redelivered.
blocks.html: This is not a promise of exactly-once processing: failures can still cause the same message to be redelivered.

blocks.text: Publish and subscribe
blocks.html: Publish and subscribe

blocks.text: To let independent services each receive an event, give each service its own queue and bind those queues to a matching exchange.
blocks.html: To let independent services each receive an event, give each service its own queue and bind those queues to a matching exchange.

blocks.text: A fanout exchange sends a copy to every bound queue. Direct or topic exchanges can give each queue only the messages matching its bindings.
blocks.html: A fanout exchange sends a copy to every bound queue. Direct or topic exchanges can give each queue only the messages matching its bindings.

blocks.text: Each service can have several competing consumers on its own queue. Pub-sub does not require exactly one consumer per queue.
blocks.html: Each service can have several competing consumers on its own queue. Pub-sub does not require exactly one consumer per queue.

blocks.text: Let us say invoice and notification services each need an order event. Each service has a queue; its own workers share the messages from that queue.
blocks.html: Let us say invoice and notification services each need an order event. Each service has a queue; its own workers share the messages from that queue.

blocks.text: Each queue has an independent acknowledgement lifecycle. Acknowledging a message in one queue does not remove the copy in another.
blocks.html: Each queue has an independent acknowledgement lifecycle. Acknowledging a message in one queue does not remove the copy in another.

blocks.text: Delivery order and processing order
blocks.html: Delivery order and processing order

blocks.text: A normal queue uses first-in, first-out delivery, but priority settings, multiple publishers, and redelivery affect the order an application observes.
blocks.html: A normal queue uses first-in, first-out delivery, but priority settings, multiple publishers, and redelivery affect the order an application observes.

blocks.text: Messages published in sequence on one channel preserve their enqueue order for a queue. Messages from different channels can interleave.
blocks.html: Messages published in sequence on one channel preserve their enqueue order for a queue. Messages from different channels can interleave.

blocks.text: Delivery order and completion order are different. Several consumers can receive messages in order but finish them in a different order.
blocks.html: Delivery order and completion order are different. Several consumers can receive messages in order but finish them in a different order.

blocks.text: Assume messages M1, M2, and M3 enter a queue in that order.
blocks.html: Assume messages M1, M2, and M3 enter a queue in that order.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ delivers M1 to consumer A and M2 to consumer B. Both deliveries are unacknowledged.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ delivers M1 to consumer A and M2 to consumer B. Both deliveries are unacknowledged.

blocks.text: Consumer B finishes M2 and acknowledges it while consumer A is still working on M1.
blocks.html: Consumer B finishes M2 and acknowledges it while consumer A is still working on M1.

blocks.text: If A then fails, M1 can be redelivered after M2 has already completed. Returning M1 to the queue cannot undo the completed work on M2.
blocks.html: If A then fails, M1 can be redelivered after M2 has already completed. Returning M1 to the queue cannot undo the completed work on M2.

blocks.text: This ordering problem does not require the requeued message to be placed at the back. Requeue placement depends on queue behaviour and concurrent activity; applications should not assume a fixed position.
blocks.html: This ordering problem does not require the requeued message to be placed at the back. Requeue placement depends on queue behaviour and concurrent activity; applications should not assume a fixed position.

blocks.text: For simpler ordered processing, use one active consumer that processes sequentially. Limiting prefetch to one also limits outstanding deliveries. Retries still need careful handling.
blocks.html: For simpler ordered processing, use one active consumer that processes sequentially. Limiting prefetch to one also limits outstanding deliveries. Retries still need careful handling.

blocks.text: Strict business ordering requires coordinating failure handling with processing. A blanket claim that all order disappears after delivery is misleading.
blocks.html: Strict business ordering requires coordinating failure handling with processing. A blanket claim that all order disappears after delivery is misleading.

blocks.text: Queues, streams, and replay
blocks.html: Queues, streams, and replay

blocks.text: In a regular queue, acknowledging a delivery allows that queue’s copy to be removed. It is not then available for replay from that queue.
blocks.html: In a regular queue, acknowledging a delivery allows that queue’s copy to be removed. It is not then available for replay from that queue.

blocks.text: This queue behaviour does not restrict the message body: messages can contain events, logs, or other application data.
blocks.html: This queue behaviour does not restrict the message body: messages can contain events, logs, or other application data.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ also provides streams: retained, append-only message storage that supports repeated reads from a chosen position.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ also provides streams: retained, append-only message storage that supports repeated reads from a chosen position.

blocks.text: Streams keep messages according to retention rules rather than removing them because one consumer read them. Independent readers can track their own positions.
blocks.html: Streams keep messages according to retention rules rather than removing them because one consumer read them. Independent readers can track their own positions.

blocks.text: Use queues for distributing pending work and routing deliveries. Consider streams when retained history and replay are part of the requirement.
blocks.html: Use queues for distributing pending work and routing deliveries. Consider streams when retained history and replay are part of the requirement.

blocks.text: Where RabbitMQ fits
blocks.html: Where RabbitMQ fits

blocks.text: Queues suit background jobs such as email delivery, image resizing, invoice generation, and order or payment workflows.
blocks.html: Queues suit background jobs such as email delivery, image resizing, invoice generation, and order or payment workflows.

blocks.text: Exchanges suit selective routing and publishing events to several independent services.
blocks.html: Exchanges suit selective routing and publishing events to several independent services.

blocks.text: Buffering lets producers and consumers run at different speeds, but queues need capacity limits and monitoring so backlogs remain manageable.
blocks.html: Buffering lets producers and consumers run at different speeds, but queues need capacity limits and monitoring so backlogs remain manageable.

blocks.text: Work that must never have a repeated business effect needs safe retries and application-level coordination. Choosing RabbitMQ does not make it run exactly once or within a guaranteed time.
blocks.html: Work that must never have a repeated business effect needs safe retries and application-level coordination. Choosing RabbitMQ does not make it run exactly once or within a guaranteed time.

blocks.text: For analytics, retained event history, or stream processing, assess RabbitMQ streams and the required retention, throughput, and processing behaviour. These requirements cannot be ruled out solely because the product is RabbitMQ.
blocks.html: For analytics, retained event history, or stream processing, assess RabbitMQ streams and the required retention, throughput, and processing behaviour. These requirements cannot be ruled out solely because the product is RabbitMQ.
